BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Gather your bits.

Tick things off as you get ready.

A note for grown-ups

Use washable child-safe paint with a grown-up. Keep paint away from your mouth and eyes. Wash hands afterward. Keep devices dry and away from paint. A grown-up should cut the matching cards.

A little more guidance ↗
ONE STEP AT A TIME

Let's make it happen.

  1. Prepare your space

    Cover the table and choose washable paints with a grown-up. Keep your device away from the paint and water.

  2. Predict a mixture

    Choose two colours. Draw or name what you think they might make before mixing.

  3. Mix small amounts

    Put a little of each paint into one tray space and mix gently. Observe the actual colour.

  4. Record the result

    Paint a sample on paper. Describe or name it in the results sheet. Clean your brush before the next mixture.

  5. Change and create

    Add more of one paint to explore a different shade. Name your own mixture and use it in a picture. Wash hands and clean the table afterward.

THE LITTLE BIT OF LEARNING

What's happening here?

Paint mixtures depend on the pigments and their proportions. Common classroom red, yellow and blue mixtures can produce orange, green and purple, but real results vary. Watching and describing your own mixture is more useful than trying to match an exact screen colour.

Keep the wondering going.

  • Which result surprised you?
  • What changed when you added more of one paint?
  • What name would you give your colour?

Make it work for you.

Keep it simple

Offer two paints at a time and let the child describe the result aloud. A grown-up can write their words.

Take it further

Compare mixtures made with different proportions. Record which paint you added more of and describe the change.

Not quite going to plan?

If a colour looks muddy, try a clean tray space and brush. Some pigments make duller mixtures; record that honestly rather than treating it as a failure.
